issues.failure_explanation: The proof equates \|M[-1;ŷ]\|_2 with berr_{A,b}(x̂) = \|Ax̂-b\|/(\|A\|_2\|x̂\|), but \|M[-1;ŷ]\|_2 = \|Ax̂-b\|_2 = \|A\|_2\|x̂\|\,\mathrm{berr}(x̂). The missing factor 1/\|A\|_2 propagates: λ_min equals \|A\|_2^2\,\mathrm{berr}(x_k)^2 (not \mathrm{berr}(x_k)^2); σ_min(T̃_k) equals \|A\|_2\,\mathrm{berr}(x_k) (not \mathrm{berr}(x_k)); and berr(x̂) equals \|T̃_k v̂\|/(\|A\|_2\|v̂\|) (not \|T̃_k v̂\|/\|v̂\|). The formula is correct only when \|A\|_2 = 1, which is not assumed.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Divide all backward-error formulas by \|A\|_2 (equivalently normalize \|A\|_2 = 1 before the GEP analysis), and scale the convergence tolerance to ε\|A\|_2 in the Cholesky/dqds checks of Algorithms 1 and 2.
issues.overall_effect: All backward-error formulas in Lemma l:quotient and Proposition prop:minberrNE are off by a factor of \|A\|_2. Algorithms MINBERR (step 5) and MINBERR-NE (step 5) test σ_min < ε when they should test σ_min < ε\|A\|_2, so they may terminate with backward error exceeding ε when \|A\|_2 < 1 or run unnecessarily long when \|A\|_2 > 1. Corollary c:minberr's guarantee of achieving ε backward error within the stated complexity is unsupported.
issues.title: Backward error formulas in MINBERR omit 1/||A||_2 normalization
issues.why_classification: Dividing by \|A\|_2 (or normalizing \|A\|_2 = 1) is a short, local change that preserves every substantive claim, convergence rate, and the advertised O(n²/√ε) complexity; no new lemma or argument is needed.

issues.failure_explanation: From the congruence, W[0;v_min] = [α;v_min] where α = -(1/\|b\|)((T_k)_{1,1}(v_min)_1+(T_k)_{1,2}(v_min)_2). For the GEP eigenvector [-1;y] to be proportional to [α;v_min] requires y = -v_min/α, so x_k = -(1/α)Q_k v_min. The proof asserts the first element of (1/α̂)W[0;v̂] is -1, but (1/α̂)[α̂;v̂] = [1;v̂/α̂] has first element +1. Consequently the derived formula x_k = (1/α)Q_k v_min has the wrong sign, producing a vector whose backward error can far exceed the Krylov-space minimum.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Flip the sign in the solution formula: use x_k = -(1/α)Q_k v_min (equivalently, redefine α without the leading minus sign) and propagate the correction to Proposition prop:minberrNE and the output steps (step 12) of Algorithms 1 and 2.
issues.overall_effect: The output formulas in Lemma l:quotient and Proposition prop:minberrNE produce vectors with the wrong sign. Algorithms MINBERR (step 12) and MINBERR-NE (step 12) therefore output solutions with potentially large backward error instead of near-optimal ones, invalidating Theorem thm:minberrcost's (1+1/2)-approximation guarantee and Corollary c:minberr's ε-backward-error guarantee.
issues.title: Sign error in MINBERR solution formula
issues.why_classification: A single sign correction in one derivation step, propagated mechanically to the lemma statement, proposition, and two algorithm output lines, preserves every claim and guarantee; no new argument is required.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: In particular, for a $1/2$-relative error ($\Delta = 0.5$), we require $\ell \geq 2.23 \ln(n/\delta^2)$.

issues.failure_explanation: Lemma lemma:invit gives the exact requirement ℓ ≥ (1/2)[1 + ln(32n ln(2/δ)/(πδ²Δ))/ln(1+Δ/2)]. Substituting Δ = 1/2 and n = k yields ℓ ≈ 2.24 ln(k/δ²) + 2.24 ln(64 ln(2/δ)/π) + 0.5, which strictly exceeds 2.23 ln(k/δ²). The simplification drops the additive constant and the log-log term, underestimating the required iterations. Thus 2.23 ln(k/δ²) steps do not guarantee Δ = 1/2 accuracy.

failure_location.quote: $\ell \geq 2.23 \ln(k / \delta^2)$ steps of inverse iteration suffice to get $\Delta=1/2$ relative accuracy

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace 2.23 ln(k/δ²) with the exact bound from Lemma lemma:invit at Δ = 1/2 (or any valid upper bound that retains the additive and log-log terms) in the proof of Theorem thm:minberrcost and in Algorithm 1's loop condition.
issues.overall_effect: The (1+1/2)-approximation guarantee in Theorem thm:minberrcost is unsupported at the stated iteration count. Algorithm MINBERR's inverse-iteration loop (step 7) may terminate before achieving the Rayleigh-quotient accuracy needed for the claimed constant-factor approximation.
issues.title: Insufficient inverse-iteration count in MINBERR complexity analysis
issues.why_classification: The exact bound is already proved in Lemma lemma:invit; substituting it (or a slightly larger constant) is a local correction that preserves the asymptotic O(k log(k/δ)) cost and all guarantees with no new argument.
